name: Black nationalism
summary: Black nationalism holds that people of African descent form a distinct nation with a right to self-determination, community control of their own politics and economy, and pride in Black history and culture. Strands range from Garvey's back-to-Africa program to Malcolm X's call for community control and self-defense and the Panthers' revolutionary socialist version; it rejects integration as dependence on white institutions and treats racial redress as owed.
scope: The mainstream twentieth-century American strand: Marcus Garvey and the UNIA's 1920 Declaration of Rights, Malcolm X's 1964 Ballot or the Bullet, and the 1966 Black Panther Ten-Point Program, as described in Wikipedia's overview. It excludes Black supremacist doctrine and religions such as the Nation of Islam's teachings on race. Economic, religious and gender answers vary by strand and most are inferred at low confidence.

sources.usedFor: Garveyite claims on rights, self-defense, Africa, segregation, education and armed service.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Adherents split between Garvey-style Black capitalism and Marxist-Leninist Panthers, so no single answer holds.

public-ownership.rationale: The Panthers wanted means of production placed in community hands, but other strands favor private Black business, so the strands divide.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The Panther program says employers who fail to provide full employment should lose control of production, implying tighter control of firms.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Malcolm X lists drug addiction among evils the Black community must clean up itself, implying opposition to legal recreational use.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The Declaration affirms free speech yet protests defamation of Black people, so adherents pull both ways.

strong-leader.rationale: Garvey's UNIA claimed a provisional leader of the Black race, but other strands favor community democracy; not clearly settled.

limit-guns.rationale: The Panther program invokes the Second Amendment for armed self-defense and Malcolm X endorsed owning rifles and shotguns.

empower-police-military.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.

reviewHistory.rationale: The Panther program centers ending police brutality and murder of Black people, so more police power is firmly opposed.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.

decide-locally.rationale: Malcolm X defines freedom as communities controlling their own politics and economy, favoring local control.

traditional-family.rationale: Cultural nationalists such as Karenga's US Organization assigned distinct family roles; strands differ and sources give little detail.

more-religion-public.rationale: Malcolm X wants all faiths united behind nationalism, but Marxist strands are secular; split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The Panther program demands reparations of land and money for slavery and exploitation, and Malcolm X insists on redress.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Pride in Black culture and achievement is described as a core belief, with Black history teaching demanded by the Panthers.

gradual-change.rationale: Malcolm X rejects patient appeals to white conscience and the Declaration justifies forceful resistance.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The Declaration rejects the League of Nations for Black people, yet Malcolm X later appealed to the UN; no settled view.

revolution-justified.rationale: The Declaration justifies resisting oppression with force and the Panther program echoes the right to dissolve destructive governments.

central-planning.rationale: Panther Marxism and Garvey capitalism pull apart.

basic-income.rationale: The Panther program demands that government guarantee every person a job or guaranteed income.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Panthers wanted state aid for cooperatives but other strands rely on private enterprise.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Malcolm X urges Black people to own their stores and businesses, favoring spread of small ownership.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Programs demand jobs and income, not abolition of wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions are absent from the sources; the nearest concern is Black-owned banks, not abolishing central banks.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Declaration demands the right to elect representatives and Malcolm X endorses the ballot.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Declaration invokes the Declaration of Independence and elected representation, not hereditary rule.

democracy-best.rationale: Malcolm X calls the ballot a weapon and the Declaration claims the right to elect representatives.

right-to-secede.rationale: Separatist strands such as the Nation of Islam discussed a separate Black state in the South, supporting secession.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Declaration asserts the right to resist oppression by force and the Panthers vowed to protect the community by whatever means necessary.

war-builds-character.rationale: The Declaration discourages Black men from serving imperial armies, implying no celebration of war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Malcolm X draws on religion and welcomes all faiths, while Marxist strands are secular.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The Panthers demand juries of peers and public accountability, not private provision.

military-superiority.rationale: The Panthers and the Declaration oppose service in the national military, so superiority is not a goal.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Core belief treats people of African descent as a single nation with a claim to self-governance.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Revolutionary nationalists take Marxist views; cultural nationalists stress race instead.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The Declaration lists colonization of Africa as a grievance and claims African land for Africans and the diaspora.

civilizational-union.rationale: The movement overlaps with Pan-Africanism and treats dispersed Africans as one people.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Adherents stress solidarity and collective self-reliance over individual selfishness.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Karenga's Kawaida stresses duties but others stress rights; unresolved.

limit-population.rationale: Not directly discussed; a movement seeking nation-building would be wary of limiting Black population growth.

restore-past-order.rationale: Adherents seek transformation of the present order of white control, not a restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Strands are strongly ideological in different ways, and the sources give no view on pragmatism versus ideology.

direct-action.rationale: Malcolm X pairs the ballot with the bullet and the Panthers used armed patrols, so adherents use both routes.

means-match-ends.rationale: Malcolm X's ballot-and-bullet pragmatism and the Panthers' armed patrols do not settle whether means must mirror ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Nothing in the movement supports it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Panther programs ask for jobs and production under community control, not abolition of specialization.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Panther demands include bread and housing but sources do not endorse need-based distribution generally.

production-for-use.rationale: Marxist strands favor it; capitalist nationalists do not.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Panther program demands an end to capitalist exploitation of the Black community and Malcolm X condemns unpaid Black labor.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Panthers were Marxist-Leninist but their program stresses community control by Black people, not class dictatorship.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Revolutionary strands drew on Mao and Fanon but others do not hold this.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Declaration objects to taxation without representation, not taxation itself.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Core belief is a collective claim to nationhood and self-governance by Black people.

conscription.rationale: The Panther program demands exemption of Black men from military service and the Declaration discourages serving imperial armies.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Emigration advocates and nation-within-a-nation advocates differ.

state-as-business.rationale: Panthers want state accountable to community needs, not run as business.

positive-liberty.rationale: Malcolm X ties freedom to political, economic and social control of the community.

total-state.rationale: Self-reliance and community control oppose a state directing all of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Ethiopianism and Garveyism speak of Africa's coming greatness and racial uplift.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Claims are for return of African land and self-determination, not expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Declaration appeals to elected representation and equal law.

bound-labor.rationale: Movement grew from resistance to slavery and peonage-like labor, so bound labor is firmly rejected.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Panther demand for education in the true history of Black people presumes mainstream teaching reflects who holds power.

universal-morality.rationale: Nothing in the sources commits adherents on universal reason-based morality; religious and secular strands differ.

single-common-good.rationale: Sources describe interest-based Black community politics but do not address whether politics has one rationally found common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Garveyism was partly inspired by Zionism, but some nationalists have been hostile; adherents split.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The Declaration says the African diaspora has a stake in Africa and claims African land for Africans at home and abroad.

economic-freedom.rationale: Malcolm X wants Black ownership of business but does not frame freedom this way.

rule-by-example.rationale: Declaration relies on laws and legal rights.

national-self-determination.rationale: The first Panther point demands power to determine the destiny of the Black community and the movement seeks representation as a nation.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Religion plays a central role for Malcolm X and the Nation of Islam.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The Declaration extends rights beyond nation-state borders.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Panther programs demand guaranteed income and survival programs without work tests.

class-collaboration.rationale: Panther class struggle stands against capitalist Black nationalists; adherents split.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Panthers demand education in Black heritage; not destroying culture.

dominated-front.rationale: Revolutionary nationalists drew on Fanon, Mao and Nkrumah and Pan-African groups link worldwide.

workers-nation.rationale: Revolutionary strands drew on international class thinking while cultural nationalists organize by race; no common answer.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Karenga's US Organization assigned distinct roles while Black feminists and many Panthers challenged them.

ban-interest.rationale: Malcolm X wants Black banks, implying lending is acceptable.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Declaration protests separate and inferior facilities and Malcolm X defines segregation as outside control, not voluntary separation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Panther Marxism and Malcolm X's complaint of outside control describe the state as a tool of the dominant.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is absent from the documented positions.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Movement rejects integration and assimilation as a goal for Black people.

national-mission.rationale: Adherents want self-determination, not spreading a government to others.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Black feminists said movements were sexist while some nationalists stress race first.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Malcolm X calls America's conscience bankrupt and attacks political delay of civil rights by the major parties.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is inconsistent with the movement's stress on dignity.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The Panther program demands an end to police murder and brutality.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Panther demands for jobs, housing and education require an active state.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Declaration asserts equal rights before the law for all and Black people's right to life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Panther program echoes the Declaration of Independence's right to dissolve destructive government and the UNIA Declaration protests taxation without representation.

population-transfer.rationale: Adherents sought voluntary emigration, not coerced removal of minorities.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Panthers framed force as defensive but accepted resistance by any means.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Black organisations have been targeted by state bans and repression.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Malcolm X says a community is segregated when outsiders control it, which echoes domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Declaration and Panther texts invoke founding rights but do not discuss the structure of divided government.

vanguard-party.rationale: Panthers followed Leninist ideas while cultural nationalists did not.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Panther program prioritises housing, bread and jobs for poor Black communities.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Panthers favored housing cooperatives but not individual purchase.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Panthers blame exploitation and institutions for poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Separatists see value in separation but others seek multi-racial coalitions.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Selection by lot is not found in any nationalist source; elections are assumed.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The Panther program demands fair trial and juries of peers because Black people have suffered from legal abuses.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Declaration affirms freedom of speech.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The Declaration claims free movement and rights for all.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Panthers were organized hierarchically while other strands were loose, and the sources give no common rule.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Pan-African unity favors union but sovereignty emphasis opposes it.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The Declaration affirms freedom of speech.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Panthers opposed military service and the Declaration discourages imperial armies.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Panthers proposed cooperative housing, not mandatory ownership.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Panthers urged armed community self-defense under the Second Amendment.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The urban Black communities central to Malcolm X and the Panthers are not contrasted with rural life in the sources.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Pan-African solidarity favors unity across borders drawn by colonizers.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Nationalists criticize white academia and Black moderates but also build educational institutions, so no clear stance.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Panthers wanted real history and knowledge in education.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Malcolm X names moral decay among evils to confront.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Cultural nationalism stresses unity and shared standards.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Malcolm X says political freedom without economic control is empty and Panthers demand community ownership.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The Declaration affirms freedoms of speech, religion and commerce.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear policy is absent from the sources.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Religion is a community institution for Malcolm X.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Separatists claim the right to a separate territory.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Inconsistent with stress on equal rights.

character-from-environment.rationale: Malcolm X blames social degradation and oppression for conditions in the community.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Declaration demands equal legal rights and fair trials.

leader-cult.rationale: UNIA treated Garvey as a recognised leader but other strands do not.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is outside the sources, and gender-role strands differ.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Panther program demands land as reparation and the Black nationalist heritage includes demand for land.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Malcolm X says religion should not divide.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The Declaration claims a single Black nation and Pan-Africanism treats Africans worldwide as one people.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The later nation-within-a-nation approach seeks self-governing institutions within the existing state.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The movement is divided between emigration to Africa and the nation-within-a-nation approach.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: As a minority, adherents rely on courts and amendments; majority-rule override is feared.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Self-reliance targets the Black community, not a closed colonial bloc.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Panther armed patrols but not clear adoption of foco theory.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The Panther program demands education in the true history of Black people and the Declaration says Black children should learn Black history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Declaration lists colonization of Africa among grievances.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Declaration adopts a flag and anthem for the Black race, implying loyalty teaching for the Black nation.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The Panther program demands reparations, so racial remedies are favored.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Panther Marxism holds crisis claims while Black capitalists do not; the sources give no common answer.

delink-world-market.rationale: Garvey's trade ambitions and Panther anti-imperialism pull in opposite directions on integration into the world market.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The Declaration protests discrimination in jobs and public facilities.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Panthers cite the Second and Fourteenth Amendments and Declaration invokes the founding rights.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Declaration claims the right to elect representatives.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Panther preamble asserts the right to abolish destructive government and the Declaration justifies resistance.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary versus monarchical authority is not a nationalist concern in the sources.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics are absent from the movement's documented positions.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Malcolm X urges using political power.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Revolutionary nationalists drew on Fanon and Nkrumah's analyses of colonial extraction.

native-born-offices.rationale: Diaspora claims on African citizenship contradict it.

party-own-road.rationale: Revolutionary nationalists built independent movements drawing on varied thinkers.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Self-reliance and self-sufficiency are core stressed beliefs.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Malcolm X describes unrequited Black labor as history; the claim is denial of slavery's role.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The sources focus on race, and Black feminist critique makes gender questions contested.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Afrocentric and nationalist strands seek institutions of their own.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Panthers oppose military and police power.

filial-duty.rationale: Cultural nationalists stress family and community duty.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Panthers cooperative land but not use-based tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Declaration protests taxation without representation.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Panthers attribute inequality to systemic injustice not just intent.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about status seeking rather than the pursuit of possessions, which is what the statement now asks about.

reviewHistory.rationale: Malcolm X urges self-discipline and community building over status seeking.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Anti-colonial rejection of imposing control on others.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local community control of economy and land supports limits on outside purchase.

job-guarantee.rationale: The Panther program says government should guarantee each person a job or income.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Malcolm X says the government is unwilling to protect Black people, weakening duty to obey.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Some nationalists promoted antisemitism, but typical adherents disclaim it.

informal-organisation.rationale: Panthers and UNIA built formal organisations.

local-production.rationale: Black-owned stores and businesses serving the community.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Declaration appeals to international rights over national law.

religious-nation.rationale: Malcolm X welcomes all faiths into the movement.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Opposed to subordination of Black peoples.

defeat-communism.rationale: Revolutionary strands are Marxist and others not anticommunist campaigners.

religion-illusion.rationale: Malcolm X and Nation of Islam hold religion central.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Black feminists said so; nationalists often did not.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The Panther program proposes housing and land cooperatives.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Panthers were Marxist-Leninist while Black-capitalist strands rejected communism, so a third-way claim is not shared.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The Declaration claims African land for Africans.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not a position of the movement.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Declaration affirms freedoms of speech and rights.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Malcolm X says not to argue over religious differences.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Declaration lists colonization of Africa among its grievances.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Malcolm X wants community members to control their politics.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Black feminists argued so while many nationalists stressed race.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Strands are explicitly left (Panthers) or centrist-capitalist (Garvey) and the sources contain no claim about the left-right divide.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Malcolm X and the Nation of Islam are Muslim.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Garvey's movement was Christian and Malcolm X spoke as a Muslim, but the Panthers were secular; adherents are split.

property-franchise.rationale: Malcolm X's Ballot or the Bullet and the UNIA Declaration demand full voting rights for Black people.

reification.rationale: The Panthers' Marxist strand might agree while Garveyites would not; the sources do not use the term.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Panther programme demands trial by a jury of peers and an end to arbitrary police power.

racial-franchise.rationale: Adherents want a Black self-governing community or state yet claim equal votes in America, so they are split on exclusive franchise.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Community control of institutions is central, which suits community deliberation; assemblies by lot are not mentioned.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Panther program demands an end to the robbery of the Black community by capitalists, which treats concentrated wealth as a source of domination.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The Panther program demands an end to police brutality and community control of police, not abolition of policing.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Adherents split: church-based and Garveyite strands kept male clerical leadership while Panther and later strands stressed women's equality.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Adherents split between patriarchal Garveyite and religious strands and the Panthers' later gender-equality commitments.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Garvey's UNIA had uniformed bodies but the sources do not present youth drilling as a general position.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The Panther program and nationalist demands for reparations treat past crimes against Black people as wrongs to be officially acknowledged.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Malcolm X, the Panther program and the Garveyite declaration endorse self-defence, including armed.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Black nationalism stresses a shared African heritage and history; the sources emphasise Black history and pride.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The sources note gender debates within the movement but give no common answer.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Garvey's program gathers the diaspora in Africa while cultural nationalists accept diaspora; adherents are split.

culture-before-state.rationale: Strands differ between cultural nationalists and political separatists.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Separatist strands and the Panther plebiscite demand a Black territory, while cultural strands do not; split.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The Panthers' revolutionary socialist version points this way, but Garvey's capitalist-leaning strand does not, so mild support.

municipal-property.rationale: Malcolm X and the Panthers called for community control of the economy of Black neighbourhoods; ownership forms vary by strand.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Garvey's UNIA and the Nation of Islam strand were religious, but the Panther strand was secular, so mild support.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The overview and Garvey's Declaration treat people of African descent as a nation with distinct interests that should be organised and defended.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in Black history, culture and heritage is a defining theme in the overview and the Declaration of Rights.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Strands differ on gender, with male-led organizations often restricting women's roles while Panther women held leadership posts, so no single answer holds.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Malcolm X and the Panther program defend armed community self-defense against police and white violence, so an adherent rejects a state-only monopoly on arms.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The Panther program demands exemption of Black men from military service in a racist government's wars, and Malcolm X opposed fighting for white America, though Garvey's UNIA supported Black armed service.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Strands differ: the Panthers sought revolution, Malcolm X posed ballot or bullet, and Garveyites built parallel institutions and looked to Africa.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about a people treated as a colony, not about regions, and the statement now asks whether richer regions owe their wealth to exploiting poorer ones.

reviewHistory.rationale: Malcolm X and the Panthers describe the Black community as economically and politically controlled by outsiders who take its wealth, the internal colony thesis of Black Power.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about a people treated as a colony, not about regions, and the statement now asks whether richer regions owe their wealth to exploiting poorer ones.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Strands differ, from Garvey's Christianity to Malcolm X's Sunni Islam and the secular Panthers, and none of the sources takes a position on a shared truth behind religions.

workers-own-party.rationale: Malcolm X urged Black communities to organize independent political power outside the two established parties, and the Panthers built their own party.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The ideology has no stated view on how regional language varieties are named; adherents are indifferent or split.

race-social-construct.rationale: Strands split: Garveyite race-first thought and Nation of Islam doctrine treat race as real, while Black Power writers framed Black people as a nation made by shared history and oppression.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The Panther program demands an end to police brutality and trial by a jury of peers, which rules out killing without trial.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The Panther program demands full employment and housing but does not say whether aid should be targeted or universal.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Garveyism blends modern progress with African heritage while other strands focus on modern politics; adherents split.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Malcolm X and the Panther program describe racism and white control as the central, continuing obstacle.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Socialist strands such as the Panthers lean toward it, while Garveyite strands do not; adherents are split.

material-over-identity.rationale: The movement is organised around racial identity, history and culture as the basis of politics, rejecting class-first or integrationist framing.

police-more-powers.rationale: The Panther program centers ending police brutality and murder of Black people, so more police power is firmly opposed. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: Anti-colonial view opposes ex-imperial influence. (Carried over from former-empire-influence, "A country should cultivate political and cultural influence in regions once ruled by its predecessor empire.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Communities should control the schools, businesses and political offices that serve them, rather than outsiders.
missingStatements.rationale: Malcolm X defines segregation as outside control of a community's politics and economy and makes community control the core of his program.

missingStatements.text: A minority facing violence from the state has the right to defend itself with arms.
missingStatements.rationale: The Panther program and Malcolm X endorse armed self-defense under the Second Amendment against police violence.

notes: Strands diverge sharply: separatist and Africa-emigration nationalists, cultural nationalists, and Marxist-Leninist revolutionary nationalists. Several 0 and low answers reflect that split. The Wikipedia summary of the 1920 Declaration is used in place of the full text.
